$comment: Self-derived finetype drift contract for usitc/hts, checked by the in-engine finetype_validate@1 gate (the model-free `ft_validate` DuckDB table macro). ft_validate MELTS every column to VARCHAR, so this contract uses ONLY the string-surviving JSON-Schema keywords. ENFORCED: the closed `enum` domains on level and text_source; the `pattern` on code: digits only at 2, 4, 6, 8 or 10 digits, length 2 to 10, the shape descriptor.overrides.json publishes; on code_display, which is dotted: finetype's canonical `geography.transportation.hs_code` validation pattern (`^\d{4}\.?\d{2}(\.?\d{2}){0,2}$`, which admits 6, 8 and 10 digits with or without dots but lacks the 2-digit chapter and 4-digit heading forms) widened by `|^[0-9]{2}$|^[0-9]{4}$`, as describe widens it in the descriptor; on rate_from_code, 6, 8 or 10 digits and nothing else, length 6 to 10, since only a subheading, tariff line or statistical line prints the rates it points at; `^[0-9]+$` on parent_code; and `minLength`/`maxLength` envelopes elsewhere. NOT ENFORCED, by design: numeric ranges (a numeric `type` BACKFIRES to 100% reject once melted to VARCHAR); NULLs (invisible to ft_validate); object-level `required` (documentation only); and the arrays `units` and `footnotes`, which do not melt to a string shape. Free-text fields (description, description_full, corpus, the rates) carry LOOSE length envelopes with generous headroom, not tight formats. Derived from build/hts.parquet: a pass-through on today's 42,036 rows, a fail-closed tripwire for future drift (an unknown level or text_source, a malformed code).
